region3_this_session.ground_truth_method: candidate-show's own .s reassembly could not resolve Region_080ddb34's literal pool (no .word data in the fragment file -- the pool lives past the fragment's own end, per CONTRIBUTING.md's 'gap between two fragment files' case). Read it straight out of the ROM instead: `arm-none-eabi-objdump -D -b binary -m arm --adjust-vma=0x08000000 -Mforce-thumb --start-address=0x080ddb34 --stop-address=0x080ddde0 roms/gs1-en.gba`, plus a raw little-endian word dump of 0x080dddb8..0x080ddddc for the pool bytes themselves (objdump misdecodes the pool as bogus Thumb2 instructions when printed inline). Also re-ran the same disassembly over 080dda3c.s's own range (0x080dda3c..0x080ddb34) to get the exact address and byte shape of `sub_080ddaba` (a local label inside the continuation file, at 0x080ddaba, not a separate region) -- this resolved the true per-frame loop body boundary, which sits between the once-only fade_start/end_wait setup (0x080ddab0..0x080ddab8) and Region_080ddb34's release/retire logic.
corrections_to_prior_placeholder: Blend condition was inverted: real ASM (`cmp r4,r6; blt .L_080ddae4`) skips the BLDCNT/BLDALPHA fade write when frame < end_wait, i.e. the write happens when frame >= end_wait. The prior candidate and this session's initial draft both had `if (frame < end_wait)`; fixed to `if (frame >= end_wait)`.

The release-scan/retire-scan block is NOT gated as a whole by `Data_080eebb6[table->24] != 0` -- only the release+retire LOOP is skipped when that gate is 0 (continuation jumps straight to `sub_080ddcda`, the interpolation loop entry, in that case). The interpolation loop over the 64-slot particle array at 0x02010000, plus the Func_080e155c/Func_080cd52c/work->0x7824=1/Func_080030f8(1) tail, run unconditionally every frame regardless of the gate. The prior placeholder wrapped everything (including the interpolation loop) inside the gate check -- restructured so only the release/retire while-loop is conditional.

The retire/announce scan (loop over table->20 members, calling Func_080f9010(132)+Func_080d6888(table->[36+2*i],7,5,i,3) when frame==announce_frame) is a SEPARATE, much simpler shape than the prior placeholder's do-while-over-64-particle-slots -- the real loop only iterates over `i` in [0,table->20), reading a single s16 member id per i from the table, with the announce condition (frame==a single scalar announce_frame, not per-member) shared across all i. The 64-particle-slot scan in the prior placeholder does not exist in this loop; it belongs to the separate interpolation loop after the release/retire portion.

Added the missing particle-spawn block (frame < release_threshold+3): scans the 64-slot particle array at 0x02010000 for a free slot (particle[6]==-1), and on finding one, sets particle[0]=clamp(*release_flag_ptr + (rng()&31) + 32, max 96), particle[1]=(rng()&31)+72, particle[6]=0. This block was entirely absent from the prior placeholder.
Added the missing one-time flag write `work->0x77a8 = 3` when frame==release_threshold+1 (was entirely absent).

Added the real dual-draw-function release logic: Data_080eeba6[release_count] selects Func_080072fc (value<=1) vs Func_080072f4 (value>1); bit 0 of that same byte then selects the +/- sign on the x argument and (for the >1 branch) which of two fixed byte offsets (0xF00=3840 vs 0x6C0=1728 from `work`) forms the src pointer. Both geometry variants (16x/6x-scaled window clamped to 80/30, vs 8x/1x-scaled window clamped to 64/8) were read directly from ROM and transcribed with their real clamp constants -- the prior placeholder had invented zero-valued x/y/w/h and a single draw call.

Added the real 64-slot interpolation loop (label 0x080ddcda onward): for each particle with state (offset 24) >= 0, half=state/2 indexes three ROM tables (Data_080eebc8 u16 src-offset, Data_080eebc0 signed byte 'amplitude A', Data_080eebb9 signed byte 'amplitude C'); two Func_080072f4 calls draw the particle offset by valC/halfA and un-offset, respectively; state increments and resets to -1 at 14. This subsystem did not exist at all in the prior placeholder.
region3_this_session.unresolved_residual: Every Func_080072fc/Func_080072f4 call site in the reference loads a 7th value into r6 immediately before the `bl` (the currently-selected draw_cb_46/draw_cb_47 heap-cache function pointer) in addition to the 6 args actually placed in r0-r3/sp+0/sp+4. r6 is not an APCS argument register for a 6-arg call and the project rule forbids forced registers / inline asm, so this session declared both functions with 6 params only and dropped the r6 value -- documented in the .c file's own comment above the prototypes. resolved_literal_pools.resolution_method: Hand pc-relative arithmetic against each .s file's own instruction stream, cross-checked with `arm-none-eabi-as -mthumb` + `arm-none-eabi-ld -Ttext=<addr>` + `objdump -d --adjust-vma=<addr>` standalone reassembly of each region. Caveat: the reassembly widened the two 080dd9c0.s branches to .set absolute symbols (bne/b to sub_080dda3c) into 4-byte bne.w/b.w forms, which shifts the tool's own computed addresses for the final BG2X pool pair by 4 bytes versus the ROM's real narrow encoding; the given LiteralPool_080dda18 label position (consistent with narrow branches, i.e. the real ROM encoding) was used as ground truth for that pair instead of the widened reassembly's arithmetic. 080dda3c.s and 080ddb34.s branch only to near local labels (no cross-file .set targets before the pool), so their reassembly address arithmetic is trusted directly.

The established idiom for this exact situation already exists in this owner's own family: games/gs1/recon/en/main/080d85d0.c line 99 spells its analogous Func_080e0524 first argument as `(s32) &Value_00000073` (an address-of a placeholder extern byte whose 'address' equals the constant, forcing a pc-relative/pool load pattern GCC cannot fold to an immediate). Applied the same idiom here: added `extern u8 Value_0000007e;` and changed the call to `Func_080e0524((s32) &Value_0000007e, work, 1, 1);`. This fixed the missing ldr, and cascaded to fix the previously-misaligned bne.n branch target and the literal-pool byte disassembly immediately following the call (both now match reference exactly) -- confirmed via re-score (dh 460->444, wrong_instructions 514->516 [noise], candidate_bytes 1008->1012).
